purpose: Contextualize existing synthetic-versus-real discrepancies using repeated community-disjoint splits of the same already exposed selected CHNS sample. No equivalence, clinical validation, population truth or generator tuning claim.

sampling.partition: Uniform random permutation of sorted community IDs; first 109 communities R1, remaining109 R2; reject only if either side has fewer than3000 eligible people.
sampling.within_side: Uniform sample without replacement of3000 eligible rows on each side; no outcome-based balancing; no person or community overlap.
sampling.exhaustion: Stop with explicit failed seed; no replacement seed or relaxed eligibility. Post-selection unavailable metrics remain null with reasons; never replace a split based on its results.
sampling.scope: Repeated splits of one fixed finite sample; no national survey-representative or independent-cohort interpretation.
sampling.indices: Sample R1 then R2 with the same per-seed PCG64 stream; sort selected row positions before analysis. Hash domain-labelled little-endian uint64 row positions; publish hashes, never membership lists.

metrics.intervals: No new confidence intervals, significance classification or multiple-testing claims. Historical intervals unchanged.

comparisons.real_real: R1-R2 signed and absolute, per split.
comparisons.generated_real: G-R2 signed and absolute, each fixed generated seed separately.
comparisons.generated_real_symmetric: (|G-R1|+|G-R2|)/2 for each split and each fixed G; removes reference-role arbitrariness but does not correct finite-sample dependence.
comparisons.report_units: Original units for signed, absolute and symmetric absolute discrepancies.
comparisons.purpose: A conditional descriptive scale comparison, not a calibrated equivalence test.

budget.independent_recalculation: One independent full check of split construction,36 metrics, all summaries and frozen-input invariance.

limitations: Same-cohort resplits estimate conditional finite-sample variation, not heterogeneity across real populations.
R1 and R2 are complementary and dependent; fixed G does not share that partition dependence. Matching n does not make discrepancy distributions exchangeable.
Community allocation and within-side row subsampling preserve disjointness but are not the original survey sampling design.
Generated rows are IID under the frozen law; matching n does not match real intracommunity dependence.
Three generated draws are one model, not three independent clinical validations.
All current CHNS and generated analyses are exposed developmental results.
No scientific usefulness threshold is learned from these discrepancies; no retroactive pass/fail rule.
